title: Pirates release struggling DH Marcell Ozuna, their biggest offseason acquisition
content:
The Pittsburgh Pirates are moving on from one of their biggest offseason acquisitions, releasing designated hitter Marcell Ozuna because of the slugger’s poor production, league sources with knowledge of the matter told The Athletic on Wednesday. The sources spoke on the condition of anonymity because the move is not yet official.

Cutting Ozuna allows the Pirates to clear room on their 40-man and active rosters for outfielder/infielder Ronny Simon.

After signing a one-year, $12 million deal with the Pirates in the offseason, Ozuna hit just .203 with a .612 OPS and eight home runs in 70 games and 280 plate appearances.

Before Monday’s trade deadline, the Pirates deepened their bullpen by acquiring relievers Luke Weaver, Kirby Yates, Lake Bachar and Camilo Doval, but Pittsburgh did not supplement its lineup. The Pirates’ .656 OPS from the DH spot this season is fourth-worst in Major League Baseball, ahead of only the Arizona Diamondbacks (.616), Detroit Tigers (.604) and Kansas City Royals (.600).

Pittsburgh (57-58) is 3 1/2 games out of a wild-card spot. FanGraphs’ playoff odds give the Pirates a 20.7 percent chance to make the postseason.

The Pirates boast MLB’s fourth-best OPS (.748) overall. Their lineup is waiting on Konnor Griffin and O’Neil Cruz to return from the injured list.
